ai.description: This semi-aquatic turtle reaches 20 cm. It features a blackish-brown domed shell, yellow head stripes, and a hinged plastron that allows complete closure. It is distinguished by its dark, flat head.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cuora amboinensis* is distinguished by its high-domed, blackish-brown carapace with a distinct, prominent central keel, which is absent in most similar Indian box turtles.
ai.habitat: *Cuora amboinensis* inhabits low-lying, slow-moving freshwater bodies like marshes, swamps, and rice paddies, typically restricted to elevations below 500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Southeast Asian Box Turtle is primarily diurnal and semi-aquatic, often foraging for plants and small invertebrates in shallow, slow-moving waters or damp forests.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cuora amboinensis* is oviparous, laying clutches of 1–5 eggs. Breeding typically occurs year-round, peaking during the monsoon season in its range.
ai.distributionRemarks: In the Indian subcontinent, *Cuora amboinensis* occurs in Northeast India (Assam and surrounding states) within low-lying wetlands and tropical forest habitats.
